ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure (1), the quadrilateral ABCD and the quadrilateral AEFG are both squares. Rotate the square AEFG around point A and connect BE and CF. When points G, F, and C are collinear, as shown in Figure (2), if $AB=5$ and $AE=\sqrt{5}$, then what is the length of $BE$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In Figure (1), quadrilateral ABCD and quadrilateral AEFG are both squares. Rotate square AEFG around point A and connect BE and CF. When points G, F, and C are collinear, as shown in Figure (2), if $AB=5$ and $AE=\sqrt{5}$, what is the length of $BE$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached image contains two panels labeled (1) and (2). In both, ABCD is a large square with A at the upper-left, B at the lower-left, C at the lower-right, and D at the upper-right. A smaller tilted square AEFG shares vertex A with the large square. In Figure (2), the slanted line through C and F also passes through G, so G, F, and C are collinear, and BE is drawn. Reasoning following the assigned vector method: Let s = AE = √5. Put A at the origin, and define vectors u = AE and v = AG. Since AEFG is a square, |u| = |v| = s and u ⟂ v. Also GF is parallel to AE, so GF has the u-direction. From Figure (2), C lies beyond F on the same ray starting at G in the u-direction, so write C = v + t u with t > 0. The large square has side AB = 5, hence its diagonal AC has length 5√2. Therefore |C|^2 = |v + t u|^2 = |v|^2 + t^2|u|^2 = 5 + 5t^2 = 50. Thus t^2 + 1 = 10, so t = 3. Hence C = 3u + v. Now choose the adjacent vertex B of the large square consistent with the orientation in Figure (2). For the square with diagonal AC = 3u + v, this gives B = 2u - v. Since E = u, the vector BE is E - B = u - (2u - v) = v - u, so BE = |u - v| = √(|u|^2 + |v|^2) = √(5 + 5) = √10.
